messages:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up — how do we want the runtime capability negotiation to work between control plane and adapters for Hosted/Dedicated/Private? Two options: upfront manifest (capabilities declared) vs probe-on-connect (feature probes). Thoughts? :thinking:

alex: Quick sketch of manifest example:
```json
{
  "capabilities": ["streaming", "kv-cache", "prefix-cache", "quant-8bit", "hsm:kms"],
  "max_seq": 8192,
  "supports_model_variants": true,
  "security": {"kms": "hsm", "egress_allowed": false}
}
```

alex: If we go manifest-first, control plane can route and plan fallbacks without runtime probing.

mira: +1 for manifest-first for scheduling and billing accuracy. but: manifests get stale, adapters might over-claim. We need a TTL and revocation.

jon: probe-on-connect also okay but increases connection latency and test surface. Probes for cheap signals (streaming hook available, kv keys yes/no) could be fine.

sara: security: probes that run model inferences or open egress are a non-starter for Private. Manifest must be signed by tenant KMS or agent identity. Also include a "sensitive_features" flag so control plane won't request probes.

kevin: hybrid proposal: require a minimal signed manifest for core capabilities + an optional "soft_probe" step for non-sensitive features. version manifests with schema v1/v2. Fallback rules: control-plane should prefer manifest claims, but fall back to a safe default if probe fails.

deploy-bot: note: created rfc/handshake-proposal.md in the repo for reference — link: https://git/repo/rfcs/handshake-proposal.md :memo:

ops-bot: runbook: https://wiki/internal/runbooks/adapter-handshake (contains rollback steps & revocation playbook)

alex: Proposed minimal manifest schema (YAML):
```yaml
schema: "redwood.capability.v1"
identity: "adapter-uuid"
signature: "base64sig"
capabilities:
  - streaming
  - kv-cache
  - prefix-cache
max_seq: 8192
sensitive_features:
  - hsm:kms
```

alex: Handshake flow sketch:
1) Adapter connects, sends signed manifest.
2) Control plane verifies signature & schema. If invalid -> reject.
3) If manifest ok, control plane computes routing & allowed fallbacks.
4) For any declared "soft" features control plane MAY request a probe call; adapter can decline if "sensitive_features".
5) If probe mismatches manifest -> mark adapter as suspect and emit audit event; optionally trigger throttle.

alex: Questions: should manifest be required for all three hosting modes? my take: yes — Hosted can accept unsigned manifests for dev but prod must be signed. Dedicated/Private must require signature. thoughts +1/-1 by EOD? :clock1:

mira: +1 (plus TTL 24h + revocation endpoint)

jon: +1, recommend a lightweight health endpoint for probes (/capabilities) that returns non-sensitive boolean flags.

sara: +1, require KMS-signed manifests in Dedicated/Private, and an allowed_probers list in manifest.

kevin: +1, will draft schema PR and compatibility guide.
